title: Why are people so apprehensive about films that may be difficult or challenging to watch?

commenti.body:
You don’t understand why it might be hard to engage with a movie commonly considered one of the most disturbing of all time? Some people aren’t interested in viewing what’s portrayed in it. I personally have no interest in watching Salo (or at least not until I’ve watched thousands of other films first). 

Now as for why people are jerks to people who like it, there’s a lot of people who think because a piece of media isn’t to their taste that anyone else who likes it must have bad taste. They can’t really see outside themselves. 

I think Haneke’s “The Seventh Continent” is probably the one that I considered the most challenging film I’ve seen because one: it is at first very slow and domestic…which it uses to lull you in to a sense of comfort and at times, boredom. Two: the film uses that comfort against you and takes the film to very dark places. I think it’s a pretty incredible work of art that I respect a lot and has stayed with me since I first watched it.

i have a creeping suspicion that their reason for finding it strange that another person enjoys Salò has nothing to do with its "difficulty" and more to do with... ya know... all the stuff that happens in it

I thought this was going to be about something like Beau Is Afraid, but I mean, your average person isn’t going to like snuff, gore, or just overall unsettling content. 

I feel like the average viewer is seeking escapism, that’s why these popcorn ass superhero movies are so damn popular. Aside from being able to project our “meta truths” on the screen and be vindicated by the heroes winning and some such, people don’t want to feel bad or feel anything negative. 

I for one love movies because it can change your perspective, give you context to life, expand your views and most importantly of all, be immersed. Great films make you FEEL. Just anything. Idc what it is.

Some people think because you watch a movie where bad things happen in it, you must enjoy those bad things. They struggle to convince of any other reason someone would watch something like so just assume there isn't. Most of them only know of these movies from what is said about them too, which is a bit like the telephone game, getting distorted by all the people that talk about it differently and getting details wrong.

Everyone is different. I can't watch horror movies, even mild ones, because I will be scared for literally the rest of my life if I ever think of them again and I absolutely hate being scared. I once just read the Wikipedia description of Human Centipede and I still get sick when the thought of it intrudes into my mind.

Movies are immersive experiences. If you're sensitive, it can put you in a bad mood for days. Cynical movies like Synechdoche NY (first thing that came to mind) can make you question life and send you into a depression. My life is sad enough. I try and avoid harsh realities in my relaxation time and prefer to escape into a better place.
